hooks: The page has meaning now. But every tag is still a box, and who decides how big it really is?
You know what a box is made of. Now, where does it sit: in the flow, or lifted out of it?
Boxes can sit anywhere. How do you line a few of them up in one row without hacks?
One direction is easy. What about rows and columns at the same time?
Layouts are in place. So why does your style rule lose to someone else's?
You know who wins. How do you keep one color or size in a single place instead of fifty?
Values are shared. Now, how does the whole layout bend for a phone screen?
The page fits every screen. Last piece: how do users send data back, and who checks it?
html-css.upNext: Your page is built and styled. Next: make it come alive with a component framework like React.

hooks: You can build components with state. How do hooks give a plain function memory?
State changes trigger renders. What does React actually do with the old and new output?
Rendering is cheap but effects are not. When do they run, and why do they loop?
Effects work. How do you hand data to a deep child without passing it down ten levels?
The tree is wired up. What do you do when it gets slow?
The client app is fast. What changes when the server renders components too?
You can build it all. How do you prove it still works after the next change?
react.upNext: React is clear. Next: how apps share and cache data across many components with state management.

hooks: You can bind data to a template. Where does the logic live, and how does it get shared?
Services are injected. Many of them return streams. How do you read those without leaks?
Streams push values. How does Angular decide when to redraw the screen?
Change detection is tuned. Now, how does the user move between pages safely?
Pages navigate. How do you collect and validate what the user types?
Forms are done. How does the app talk to a real server, and who adds the token?
Data comes over HTTP. Is there a lighter way than RxJS to track state?
Signals simplify state. How do you test all of this in isolation?
angular.upNext: Angular's core is covered. Next: pick a state management approach for data shared across the whole app.

hooks: The browser has built the page. What happens when your code changes a width mid-way?
Layout work is costly. What else makes the first load heavy, and how do you ship less code?
Less JavaScript helps. Images and fonts are usually the biggest bytes left, so how do you trim them?
Assets are lean. How do you measure whether users actually feel the speed?
You have the metrics. How do you avoid downloading the same bytes twice?
Caching is set. When something is still slow, how do you find the real cause?
browser-performance.upNext: You can now speed up one page. Next: make sure everyone can use it, with web accessibility.

hooks: Four principles guide everything. What is the first, simplest way to follow them in HTML?
Native elements do most of it. When they are not enough, what does ARIA add?
Roles describe widgets. But can someone using only a keyboard reach and use them?
Keyboard users can move. Is the page still readable with low vision or motion sensitivity?
Contrast and motion are handled. How do you hear what a screen reader user hears?
Manual checks work. What can automated tools catch, and what can they not?
You know the tests. How do you say how accessible you are in contract terms?
accessibility.upNext: Accessibility is covered. Next: how to manage the state that makes interfaces dynamic.

hooks: You can name the three kinds of state. How do you decide which tool fits which?
You have a way to choose. What does Redux's strict pattern give you?
Redux is heavy for some apps. What are the lighter options?
Light tools exist. What do you give up by choosing one over Redux?
Server data behaves differently from UI state. What tool is built for it?
React Query handles server state. Does it make Redux unnecessary for that job?
Cached data goes stale. How and when do you throw it away?
Fresh data is cheap to ask for. How do you make the UI feel instant before the server answers?
